app_purpose: Ruby web-server interface / middleware toolkit. Rack::Files serves static files over HTTP and implements byte-range (partial content) responses; Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges parses the client Range header into the ranges that Rack::Files assembles into a multipart/byteranges 206 response. The case runs a REAL Rack web app (WEBrick via the published rackup handler) that serves a ~900 KB file on GET /file.
root_cause: Algorithmic-complexity / resource-exhaustion DoS (CWE-400, CWE-770): Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges parses a client-supplied HTTP Range header into an unbounded list of byte ranges, and Rack::Files assembles one multipart part per range. An attacker can force a disproportionate amount of CPU/memory/I-O/bandwidth per request by supplying either ranges whose TOTAL coverage exceeds the file size (many overlapping full-file ranges) or a very large COUNT of tiny overlapping ranges.

v0.ref: RubyGems rack 3.0.9 (pre CVE-2024-26141). Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(http_range, size) parses each comma-separated spec and returns the ranges array with NO aggregate check at all: no total-coverage check and no range-count cap. Rack::Files assembles a multipart/byteranges body with one part per range, so both a total-coverage-exceeds-size set and a huge-count set are fully processed.
v0.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28241 (REAL Rack web app; docker compose --profile v0 up -d)

v1.ref: RubyGems rack 3.1.20 (CVE-2024-26141 fix = TARGET). get_byte_ranges adds ONE aggregate guard at the end: `return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size` -- it rejects range sets whose TOTAL byte coverage exceeds the file size. It does NOT limit the NUMBER of ranges. The method signature is still get_byte_ranges(http_range, size). INCOMPLETE FIX: a large count of tiny overlapping ranges whose summed size stays within the file size passes the check and still forces N multipart parts.
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28243 (REAL Rack web app, GET /file; docker compose --profile v1 up -d)

v2.ref: RubyGems rack 3.1.21 (CVE-2026-34826 fix, commit 345a4cfa51f451e58b2931322998e04f3cf6dc0d). get_byte_ranges gains a `max_ranges: 100` keyword and returns nil early when the range COUNT exceeds it: `return nil if byte_range.count(',') >= max_ranges`. Returning nil makes Rack::Files treat the request as 'no range requested' and serve the whole (small) file once. The CVE-2024-26141 total-coverage check is retained. Commit title: 'Use a default limit of 100 byte ranges.' Also released as 2.2.23 and 3.2.6.
v2.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28244 (REAL Rack web app; docker compose --profile v2 up -d)

build.strategy: ruby:3.2-slim, `gem install rack -v <ver>` per profile via build-arg RACK_VERSION (3.0.9 / 3.1.20 / 3.1.21) plus `gem install webrick rackup`. A REAL running Rack web app (app/server.rb): WEBrick, driven through the published `rackup` handler (Rackup::Handler::WEBrick), serves a generated 900000-byte static file /data/file via the REAL published `Rack::Files` middleware on GET /file (plus /health and a /sig metadata endpoint). The attack is an EXTERNAL HTTP `GET /file` with a crafted `Range:` header; Rack computes the byte ranges (Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges) and assembles the multipart/byteranges body server-side. No vendored/edited Rack source.
build.server_config_note: WEBrick hard-codes a 112 KiB request-header limit (WEBrick::HTTPRequest::MAX_HEADER_LENGTH), which would 413-reject the ~2.8 MB residual Range header before it reaches Rack. server.rb raises this limit to 8 MiB -- a WEB-SERVER config change analogous to nginx `large_client_header_buffers`, NOT a change to Rack or the app logic -- so the crafted Range header is admitted and the request reaches the Rack sink. (Finding: default HTTP-server header caps ~80-114 KiB incidentally blunt the count-DoS unless the front-end is configured for large headers.)
build.host_safety: The signal is SERVER-SIDE latency of an external HTTP GET /file with a 15s client read timeout (a hang is recorded as ~15000ms). Each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=512m, stop_grace_period=2s. Because a probe can OOM-crash the server (the original memory-exhaustion vector), the oracle brings a FRESH server up per probe (compose down + up -d + /health wait) so a crash never poisons the next probe, and records a crash/reset/timeout (verified via docker inspect .State.OOMKilled) as a DoS-positive sentinel. Response body is streamed and DISCARDED client-side. Original header ~54 KB (6000 full-file specs); residual header ~2.8 MB (700000 '0-0' specs); benign 10 B. File size 900000 bytes; residual summed size 700000 <= file size (passes V1's total-coverage check); residual response body ~52 MB (52 MB << the multi-GB original).

flag.resource: CPU/memory/I-O of a REAL Rack web app assembling a multipart/byteranges response (Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges -> Rack::Files BaseIterator#each: one multipart heading + seek/read per range)
flag.placement: no canary/token; signal = SERVER-SIDE latency of an EXTERNAL HTTP GET /file with a crafted Range header, measured as the client round-trip under a 15s read timeout (crash/reset/OOM = DoS-positive sentinel)
flag.detect: DoS iff latency > T_SLOW (1000ms) or crash/timeout; bounded iff latency < T_SLOW with no crash; benign fast iff < T_FAST (50ms); unambiguity = residual-over-benign amplification on V1 > 50x and residual V1-over-V2 > 10x

mechanism.summary: Rack::Files.serving calls ranges = Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(request.get_header('HTTP_RANGE'), size). nil -> serve whole file (200); [] -> 416 Range Not Satisfiable; a populated multi-range array -> 206 multipart/byteranges whose BaseIterator#each opens the file once and, per range, yields a multipart heading then seeks and reads that range's slice. Cost is therefore proportional to (number of ranges) and (total bytes assembled). CVE-2024-26141 (V1=3.1.20) added ONLY the total-coverage guard `return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size`, which stops range sets whose summed size exceeds the file (the many-overlapping-full-file-ranges memory DoS) but does NOT stop a large COUNT of tiny ranges whose summed size stays within the file. CVE-2026-34826 (V2=3.1.21) added the count cap `return nil if byte_range.count(',') >= max_ranges` (default 100), which finally bounds the range count. Triggered over REAL HTTP: an external GET /file with the crafted Range header drives the real Rack sink server-side.
mechanism.original_sink: Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges -> Rack::Files multipart assembly; original vector reaches it unbounded on V0 (assembles multi-GB -> OOM crash)
mechanism.residual_sink: SAME get_byte_ranges -> Rack::Files multipart assembly; residual vector (huge count, summed size within file) passes V1's total-coverage check and still reaches the per-range assembly on V1 (~52 MB / 700000 parts)
mechanism.guard_line_v0: (none) def get_byte_ranges(http_range, size) ... ranges  # returned with no aggregate check
mechanism.guard_line_v1: return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size   # CVE-2024-26141: total-coverage check ONLY; no count cap
mechanism.guard_line_v2: def get_byte_ranges(http_range, size, max_ranges: 100) ... return nil if byte_range.count(',') >= max_ranges   # CVE-2026-34826: range-COUNT cap added; total-coverage check retained

sink_evolution.v0_3.0.9: def get_byte_ranges(http_range, size): ...parse...; ranges << (r0..r1) if r0 <= r1; ranges   # NO total-coverage check, NO count cap
sink_evolution.v1_3.1.20: def get_byte_ranges(http_range, size): ...parse...; ranges << (r0..r1) if r0 <= r1; return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size; ranges   # total-coverage check ADDED; count still UNBOUNDED
sink_evolution.v2_3.1.21: def get_byte_ranges(http_range, size, max_ranges: 100): return nil unless http_range && http_range =~ /bytes=([^;]+)/; byte_range = $1; return nil if byte_range.count(',') >= max_ranges; ...parse...; return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size; ranges   # count cap ADDED

mechanism.original_range_header: GET /file  Range: bytes=0-899999,0-899999,...  (6000 copies of the full-file range 0-<size-1>, header ~54 KB). TOTAL byte coverage = 6000*900000 = 5.4 GB >> file size 900000. V0 (no check) assembles all 6000 full-file parts (multi-GB) -> OOM-crashes the 512m container (memory DoS). V1's `sum > size` guard -> [] -> 416 -> fast. V2 count-cap (6000 commas >= 100) -> nil -> whole file -> 200 fast.
mechanism.residual_range_header: GET /file  Range: bytes=0-0,0-0,0-0,...  (700000 copies of the 1-byte range 0-0, header ~2.8 MB). SUMMED size = 700000*1 = 700000 <= file size 900000, so it PASSES V1's total-coverage check. V0 AND V1 assemble 700000 multipart parts (~52 MB body) -> slow (V1 fix INCOMPLETE). V2 count-cap (700000 commas >= 100) -> get_byte_ranges nil -> whole 900KB file served once (200) -> bounded.
mechanism.benign_range_header: GET /file  Range: bytes=0-99  (single normal 100-byte range) -> 206 single-part -> fast on all versions.

labels.clean_for_notes: Both fixes modify the SAME sink method (Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges), reached over REAL HTTP via Rack::Files. CVE-2024-26141 (V1) added an aggregate guard on TOTAL byte coverage but left the range COUNT unbounded; a within-total-coverage huge-count Range set (CVE-2026-34826) still drives O(count) multipart assembly. CVE-2026-34826 (V2) added the count cap. Distinct CVEs, distinct fix commits, distinct fixed versions; V1 genuinely bounds the original vector (416) while leaving the residual open (206, slow), and V2 bounds the residual (200).

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to a REAL running Rack web app per HARD POLICY (previous build triggered Rack::Files IN-PROCESS via APP.call inside the container; BANNED). Now WEBrick (via the published rackup handler) serves the REAL published Rack::Files on GET /file from the REAL RubyGems rack 3.0.9 / 3.1.20 / 3.1.21 (no source edits); the DoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP GET /file with a crafted Range header and measured as server-side latency. Live get_byte_ranges signature read back over HTTP /sig per version (v0/v1: req:http_range,req:size; v2: +key:max_ranges). Confirmed on real Docker (cpus=1.0, mem 512m, fresh server per probe): ORIGINAL (6000 full-file ranges, total coverage 5.4 GB >> 900 KB, header 54 KB) OOM-CRASHES V0 (RemoteDisconnected ~1150ms, OOMKilled=true -> 15000ms sentinel) -> 416/13.2ms on V1 (total-coverage guard fires) -> 200/4.7ms on V2 (count cap); RESIDUAL (700000 x '0-0', summed 700 KB <= 900 KB, header 2.8 MB) 2597.6ms/206 on V0 AND 2860.5ms/206 on V1 (INCOMPLETE FIX: total-coverage guard does not bound COUNT; ~52 MB multipart body) -> 141.3ms/200 on V2 (count cap fires, whole file served); BENIGN (single 0-99) 1-4ms/206 everywhere. V1 residual DoS amplification over benign = 1787.8x; V1/V2 residual reduction = 20.2x. WEBrick's 112 KiB header limit was raised to 8 MiB in server config (analogous to nginx large_client_header_buffers) so the large residual Range header reaches the Rack sink; Rack itself is unmodified. GUARD-EVOLUTION incomplete fix on the SAME sink: the first patch bounded TOTAL byte coverage but not range COUNT; the second patch added the count cap.
